# Summary of UKIP's 2017 Manifesto: "Britain Together"

## Core Message and Brexit Priority

UKIP positions itself as Britain's "insurance policy" and "guard dogs of Brexit," claiming to be the only party capable of delivering the genuine Brexit that 17 million voters demanded. The manifesto establishes six key Brexit tests: resumption of parliamentary legal supremacy free from European Court jurisdiction, full migration control, restoration of maritime sovereignty (200-mile exclusive economic zone), independent trade policy outside the single market and customs union, no divorce payment to the EU, and completion by end of 2019.

## Immigration and Integration

UKIP proposes reducing net migration to zero over five years through an Australian-style points-based system applied equally to all nationalities. A five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration would follow EU exit. The party emphasises integration as strongly as immigration control, proposing to disband sharia councils, ban the niqab and burqa in public places, and tackle "cultural crimes" including FGM, forced marriage, and honour-based violence with zero tolerance. The manifesto frames these positions not as discriminatory but as defending British values of equality, free speech, and democracy against practices it considers incompatible with British law.

## Economic and Fiscal Approach

The party pledges no tax increases, funding priorities through £35 billion in savings from cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, reforming the Barnett Formula, and ending EU contributions. Key proposals include raising the personal allowance to £13,500, the 40% tax threshold to £55,000, and inheritance tax threshold to £500,000. VAT would be removed from domestic energy and hot takeaway food, and the TV licence abolished. Business rates would be cut by 20% for small premises, while large multinationals would face stricter enforcement of corporation tax obligations.

## Public Services

NHS funding would increase by £11 billion annually by 2021/22, with the service restricted to British citizens and those contributing taxes for five years. Medical school places would increase, tuition fees would be scrapped for STEM students committed to working in Britain, and grammar schools would be established in every town. Social care would receive £2 billion extra annually with full NHS integration. The party promises 20,000 additional police officers, 7,000 prison officers, and 4,000 border force staff.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

UKIP commits to genuine 2% GDP defence spending plus £1 billion annually, reversing military cuts and establishing a Veterans' Administration. The party opposes military interventionism while supporting NATO and the nuclear deterrent, seeking better relations with Russia conditional on changed behaviour, and prioritising Commonwealth trade relationships.
